name: Ship or Die
tagline: A commitment device for indie builders: set a shipping deadline, log what you ship, watch the streak or the countdown judge you.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is genuinely small: a projects table, a daily check-in, a streak calculation, a countdown, maybe a webhook that nags you. An agent will hand you all of that in one sitting and it will look fine. The problem is that accountability tools are not valuable because of their features, they are valuable because you cannot quietly rewrite the record, and a personal build is a database you own with a text editor two keystrokes away. If the paid version puts money, a public profile, or other humans on the line, that part does not come out of the repo. Build it if you want the log, pay if you want the consequence.
coreLoopDIY: A local daily check-in that asks whether you shipped, stores the entry with an optional link, and renders a streak, a heatmap, and a deadline countdown.
requirements: Node and a place to run it, a laptop is fine
A Discord or Telegram webhook if you want reminders
Cron or a systemd timer for the nightly nudge
A cheap VPS or tunnel if you want the public streak page to actually be public
Enough honesty to not edit your own rows
whatYouLose: Real stakes: no payment hold, no forfeit, no penalty you actually feel
An audience: nobody is watching your streak page unless you go find them
Tamper resistance, since you own the database and the delete button
Reminders that reliably reach you on your phone without you maintaining a cron job
Whatever social scaffolding the paid product has around it, cohorts, feeds, other builders shipping at the same time
moatNotes: Commitment devices borrow their power from a third party. The third party is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the failure mode of a self-hosted accountability app is that you stop opening it and nothing happens. A paid one has a name attached, possibly your card, possibly other people who can see the gap in your log, and that asymmetry is the entire mechanism. People are not paying for a streak counter, they are paying to hand the referee whistle to someone who is not them. That said, a decent share of buyers here only ever needed a shipping journal, and a shipping journal is a one-sitting build.
notes: Easy to clone, hard to obey.
prompt:
Build a local-first shipping accountability tracker called "Ship Log".
Stack: Next.js with the App Router and TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite through better-sqlite3. No cloud services, no accounts, no telemetry.
Data model: projects (id, name, deadline, stake_note), ships (id, project_id, shipped_at, title, url, note), checkins (id, day, status one of shipped or skipped, reason).
Core loop: each day the app asks one question, "did you ship?", and takes a one line entry plus an optional link. A missing day breaks the streak and records a skip with a short reason.
Pages: /today is the single question check-in form and nothing else. /streak shows a CSS grid heatmap of the last 180 days plus current and longest streak. /projects is CRUD with a deadline countdown in days. /p/[project] is a read only page showing the streak and the last ten ships, with no edit controls rendered at all.
Add a HARD_MODE flag in .env. When it is true, past check-ins cannot be edited or deleted through the UI, only by opening the SQLite file directly. Surface that state in the header, it is the point of the app.
Reminders: an /api/cron/remind route that posts today's status to a Discord or Telegram webhook read from .env, and refuses to run without a shared secret in the query string.
Include a seed script that writes 30 days of plausible history so the heatmap is not empty on first run.
Single user only. No auth, bind to localhost by default, and say plainly in the README that the public page is only public if you put it behind a tunnel or a small VPS.
Out of scope, do not build: payments, real money stakes, email, mobile apps, multi user, leaderboards, OAuth, analytics.
Deliver a README with setup steps, a .env.example listing DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL, CRON_SECRET and HARD_MODE, and npm scripts for dev, seed and build.
Style: dark, monospace, one accent color, no chart library.
Write vitest tests for the streak calculation covering timezone edges, a skipped day in the middle, and a streak that is still open today.
